newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were mixed in a liquid market on Friday, dealers said.
"The rates are quite mixed and at the moment the market is up Z$112 million compared to yesterday's surplus of Z$300 million," one dealer said.

The dealers said discount houses were buying treasury bills at a rate of 19.73 percent and selling them at 19.50 percent following the weekly tender on Thursday. This compared with a buying rate of 20.5 percent set at last week's treasury bill auction.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at their overnight rate of 22 percent and sold at between 20 and 21 percent, marginally down on Thursday's 21.5 percent while bankers' acceptance bills were being bought at 21 percent and trading at 20 percent compared to 21.5 percent and 21 percent.
The call rate stabilised at 19 percent compared to its overnight fluctuations in a 15 to 20 percent range.
